ledger.note: 1818: the Dil brothers seize Kandahar. 'In August 1818, the Dil brothers led by Sher Dil Khan seized Kandahar and its surroundings and declared independence.'

1818: Sindh passes under Kandahar. KD says Sindh and Balochistan 'were able to break away in August 1826 following the death of Sher Dil Khan', implying the link since 1818; no page dates its start. The Durrani dossier ends its own hold on Sindh in 1818.
1818: Balochistan (Kalat) passes under Kandahar, as for Sindh: the break-away of August 1826 implies it; no page dates the start.
1826: Sindh breaks away. 'Sindh and Balochistan were able to break away in August 1826 following the death of Sher Dil Khan.'
1826: Balochistan breaks away, with Sindh, after Sher Dil Khan's death on 9 August 1826.
1839: Kandahar falls to Shah Shuja and the British. 'Fall of Kandahar: 8 May 1839'; the infobox lists the Durrani Empire (Shah Shuja) as successor in 1839.

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from two pages (KD, DM). Disagreement: KD says the principality ended with Dost Mohammad's conquest in September 1856 (the end of Rahim Dil Khan's reign), DM says 'In November 1855, he conquered Kandahar'; the emirate-of-afghanistan dossier (ia-03-e) uses 1855/11, which is followed. KD's infobox lists the Durrani Empire (Shah Shuja) as successor in 1839 and predecessor in 1842; the durrani-dynasty dossier dates Shuja's takeover to August 1839 where KD gives 8 May 1839. Not on KD: Girishk, Farah, Quetta/Shal, the infobox area. The vassal pairs for Sindh and Balochistan are confidence 1 at the start (inferred from the 1826 break-away); the Talpur and Kalat counterparts (talpur-dynasty, khanate-of-kalat) belong to the south-Asia groups. Names for the gazetteer: Sibi, Pishin, Shorawak (places in Pakistani Balochistan and Kandahar) are named in KD but are not used as regions (a Chaman radius stands in).
